questions.question_text: Find $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{-1}{\sqrt{4-x^{2}}}\,dx$, giving the answer as an inverse cosine.

options.why: Ignored the minus sign in the numerator, which is what turns $\arcsin$ into $\arccos$.
Wrote the inner function as $ax$ instead of $\dfrac{x}{a}$.
Ignored the minus sign and also wrote the inner function as $2x$ rather than $\dfrac{x}{2}$.

questions.solution_text:
Here $a=2$, and $\dfrac{-1}{\sqrt{4-x^{2}}}$ is the derivative of $\arccos\dfrac{x}{2}$.
$\displaystyle\int\dfrac{-1}{\sqrt{4-x^{2}}}\,dx=\arccos\dfrac{x}{2}+C$
